headline: voxcraft-sim at its pinned commit does NOT compile on CUDA 13.1 targeting sm_90. Two independent failures occurred in two different translation units. The FIRST error in the build is a Boost.Asio failure, not the device-synchronisation failure this packet predicted.

job.why_no_cases: the build failed, so neither the actuated nor the passive case ran. The history validator and the actuation discriminator were never exercised on this engine. logs/97-history-sha256.txt is legitimately empty and hashes to the canonical empty-input sha256.

toolchain_as_measured_on_the_node.gpu: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, driver 580.173.02, compute capability 9.0, 81559 MiB
toolchain_as_measured_on_the_node.gpu_note: compute capability 9.0 confirms sm_90 was the correct target for the forced architecture

independent_audit_performed_here.12_native_files_rehashed: 12/12 match probe-transport.json on both size and sha256; 0 mismatched
independent_audit_performed_here.hash_check_negative_control: appending one byte to 51-first-error.txt changes its digest, so the comparison can fail
independent_audit_performed_here.empty_file_control: 97-history-sha256.txt is 0 bytes and its recorded digest equals sha256 of empty input
independent_audit_performed_here.source_identity: the node fetched tarball sha256 0a0f4fd1... which equals the frozen packet pin exactly, and its 14 load-bearing files matched on the node (logs/11-verify.txt). All 403 tracked files were previously verified HERE against a git clone at dd8668f9 from that same tarball hash, 0 missing and 0 mismatched, so the 403 are covered transitively by the whole-archive digest.
independent_audit_performed_here.cmake_guard: logs/20-cmake-inspect.txt shows lines 47, 48, 54 and 60 present in the FETCHED bytes, so -DCUDA_ARCH did bypass the GPU-probing branch as the packet claimed

first_error_in_the_build.verbatim: /usr/include/boost/asio/traits/static_query.hpp:70:112: error: ‘‘indirect_ref’ not supported by dump_decl<declaration error>’ is not a template [-fpermissive]
first_error_in_the_build.kind: Boost.Asio header failing under this compiler

ACTUAL_ERROR_SEQUENCE_do_not_reorder.overlap: none; the two sets are disjoint
ACTUAL_ERROR_SEQUENCE_do_not_reorder.interleaving_note: make -j2 compiled the two translation units concurrently, so their relative position in the log is partly a scheduling artefact. What is NOT an artefact is that each unit failed for its own reason and neither failure caused the other.

failure_1_boost_IS_OUR_DEPENDENCY_CHOICE.installed_by: this packet's own adapter step, apt-get install libboost-{filesystem,thread,chrono,program_options}-dev
failure_1_boost_IS_OUR_DEPENDENCY_CHOICE.what_upstream_says: the voxcraft-sim README at this commit states 'Versions of boost known to work: 1.65.1 and 1.67.0'
failure_1_boost_IS_OUR_DEPENDENCY_CHOICE.our_error: we installed a Boost roughly sixteen minor versions newer than anything upstream claims to support, and it fails inside nvcc 13.1. That is a choice recorded in our own packet, not a property of voxcraft-sim.
failure_1_boost_IS_OUR_DEPENDENCY_CHOICE.and_we_predicted_it_for_the_WRONG_REASON: probe.json listed Boost as a possible stop, but as a CONFIGURE-time find_package failure 'before nvcc is ever invoked'. Configure succeeded. The failure is at COMPILE time, inside nvcc, on Boost.Asio headers. Right dependency, wrong stage, wrong mechanism.
failure_1_boost_IS_OUR_DEPENDENCY_CHOICE.fixable_in_principle: a Boost version within upstream's stated range might clear this one. That is a statement about this failure only and authorises nothing.

verbatim_pair: calling a __host__ function("cudaDeviceSynchronize") from a __device__ function("VX3_VoxelyzeKernel::doTimeStep") is not allowed
identifier "cudaDeviceSynchronize" is undefined in device code
failure_2_device_synchronisation_IS_UPST.NOT_CONTAMINATED_BY_BOOST: VX3_VoxelyzeKernel.cu has no Boost include at all. The only occurrence of the string 'boost' in that file is a comment at line 121 reading 'no std::, no boost::'. Its 16 errors are device-synchronisation errors and nothing else, and they fall entirely between the two make failures. So this incompatibility is established independently of the Boost problem.
failure_2_device_synchronisation_IS_UPST.mechanism: device-side cudaDeviceSynchronize was deprecated in CUDA 11.6 and removed in CUDA 12.0 with CDP2. CUDA 13.1 rejects it. This is in upstream's own source.

what_we_got_right: the mechanism: device-side cudaDeviceSynchronize is rejected by a modern toolkit, confirmed verbatim under CUDA 13.1
the exact set of 8 sites, 232/269/303/312/428/437/446/473, all present and no others
the enclosing functions named for each site
that -DCUDA_ARCH bypasses the autodetection branch, confirmed on the node
what_we_got_WRONG: probe.json declared first_site_expected = VX3_VoxelyzeKernel.cu:232. It is not the first error in the build, which is Boost.Asio 68 log lines earlier, and it is not even first among the device-sync sites: it is reported FOURTH of eight, after 269, 303 and 312.
Boost was predicted as a configure-time find_package failure; it is a compile-time nvcc failure on Asio headers, after configure succeeded.
OUR_PREDICTION_SCORED_HONESTLY.the_rule_this_obeys: the predicted failure is NOT promoted to first. The sequence is reported as the compiler produced it. A prediction that names the right mechanism and the wrong position is a partly correct prediction and is recorded as one.

what_this_result_does_and_does_not_licen.licensed: voxcraft-sim at dd8668f9, unmodified, does not compile under CUDA 13.1 for sm_90 with Boost 1.83. The device-synchronisation incompatibility is in upstream's own source and is independent of the dependency problem.
not_licensed: any statement about the engine's correctness, physics or numerical behaviour: no simulation ran
any biological or convergence claim, in either direction
that a different image or a smaller image would fix it: the CUDA API incompatibility is in upstream source, not in the environment
that our predicted first site was confirmed: it was not
what_this_result_does_and_does_not_licen.authorised_next_steps: none. No new job and no source patch is authorised by this result. Removing the device-side synchronisation would change the integration order, which is a semantic change, and a port or toolkit change would need primary-source compatibility evidence rather than flag shuffling.

defects_in_our_own_instrumentation_found.cause: our preflight regex matched 'memory.total\n' but nvidia-smi emits the header 'name, driver_version, compute_cap, memory.total [MiB]'. The ' [MiB]' suffix defeated the match.
defects_in_our_own_instrumentation_found.impact: cosmetic. The raw line 'NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, 580.173.02, 9.0, 81559 MiB' is retained verbatim in logs/00-preflight.txt, so nothing was lost.
defects_in_our_own_instrumentation_found.why_not_fixed_here: the admitted archive hash da3a6f7f is the artifact this result is attributed to. Editing adapter/ now would break that attribution for a cosmetic parser bug. It is recorded instead.

cpu_arms_unchanged: the existing CPU preregistration stands untouched, including the arm E miss at 0.0175 against a 0.01 bound, the arm G spatial non-convergence at 8.2x, and the withdrawal of the 2.74% travelling-wave figure in favour of 15.5739% at a common denominator.
